goal: Operator-directed repository release prep: collapse the entire git history into a single initial commit via an orphan branch and force-push main, then make the repository public so npm provenance publishing works.

acceptance_criteria.statement: main becomes a single root commit containing the full current tree; the remote main is force-updated to it.
The GitHub repository visibility is set to public after the collapsed history lands.
No real secrets ship in the collapsed public tree: .env is gitignored, .env.example is a template, and the only token-shaped strings are the documented synthetic test fixtures.

outcome.summary: History collapsed to one initial commit and force-pushed; the repository is public; prior commit hashes referenced by older evidence records no longer resolve (expected, operator-directed).

what_worked: The orphan-branch collapse keeps the entire current tree while dropping all prior history, which also guarantees no historical secret can leak into the public repo.
Secrets scan before going public found only the synthetic test fixtures.

calls.name: history-collapse
calls.purpose: Rebuild main as a single root commit from the current tree and force-push.

calls.name: repo-public
calls.purpose: Set the GitHub repository to public visibility.

evidence.summary: main is a single root commit after the force push.
Tracked files contain only the synthetic test fixture tokens; .env is ignored and .env.example is an empty template.

uncertainty.statement: Evidence records committed earlier reference pre-collapse commit hashes that no longer resolve.
uncertainty.resolution: Accepted as operator-directed history collapse; new records pin the new root commit.

notes: Operator explicitly requested the history collapse, force push, and public visibility.
